PURPOSE: Python sieves run over a build; reds a component that fails one (no charter, no proofs, a silent device, ...). "We find a new thing, we add a new sieve."
It outputs only its findings. It certifies nothing, records no crossing, and posts nothing; the gate consumes its findings.

It is the READY TO MERGE ONTO MAIN step of the pipeline: everything's proved, and merging implies pushing it up. With a branch per ticket (3.3.6), commits on the branch are as often as we like; the inspector is the step at ready to merge. Checking what a change touched belongs here; nothing hangs off the git post-commit hook.
bus_client: gets a process onto the bus (reach a device, or connect). Its connect is a wake attempt (5.3.5.1). USERS: every process that speaks.
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it.
